utterances.text: I think that this happened later when we were due to have a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us how it came about, will you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the meeting?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and how it was discovered that you were in this basement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Mujezinovic came, looking for people to negotiate with the HVO, that is what he told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Dr. Mujezinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time he was President of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say to him when he came? Did he come to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I would negotiate, but that UNPROFOR and the Red Cross had to be present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He left with some other people upstairs, to the upper storey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came back half an hour later and asked me to go as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually he did not come, someone else came from that service who were in that building and later I went and there was another man who went with me upstairs, to this room upstairs on the top floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went upstairs, who did you meet then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from the people who went upstairs from the basement, there were two other people, two other Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was these two other Croats that you were negotiating with, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, actually they were not real negotiations. They asked us to call the commander of the III Corps to insist that they stop operations, and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the name of the two Croat people that asked you to do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Josip Zvonko Cilic and Boro Jozic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what positions they held at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Cilic was in the information and propaganda activities and Boro Jozic was engaged in exchange of prisoners and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what organisation was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They worked for the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met them, did you ask to speak to some people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that if we were to have talks, we should have them with competent people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you name the competent people that you wanted to speak to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were Ivica Santic and Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have told us the position of Ivica Santic. What position, so far as you knew, did Skopljak hold and why did you want to speak to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, he was President of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you want to speak to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were the people who were competent and who could probably come to some sort of an agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just need to clarify: who was it that was President of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you mentioned a moment ago that you were asked to speak to the commander of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the region, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what he wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina for that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What Corps was he the commander of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the III Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the III Corps headquartered? Where was its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this where Hadzihasanovic was located as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was where he was based, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other officers in the III Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ramiz Dugalic, who was deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long had you known Ramiz Dugalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He comes from Vitez, but I know him maybe since April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently speak to Dugalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did speak to Dugalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told him where we were, that Zvonko Cilic and Boro Jozic were with us, that they were treating us quite decently, that it would be a good idea to put an end to this, that there were a lot of us captured, and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that he would see, that he would try to do something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there then a proposal that either side should sign off to an agreement to reflect what had been discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was supposed to be like some kind of an announcement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the announcement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that in the first place to put an end to hostilities, to calm people down and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it intended would be the parties to this document, this announcement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the one side those present and on the other, that is representatives of the Bosniak group and the Croatian representatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the -- can you tell us what the HZ-HB is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the HVO is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document that was proposed between you, did you sign the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well we had a talk, there were various proposals but in the end, we signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you initially refuse to sign it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a part that we could not agree with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The subordination of the BiH army in Vitez to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why could you not agree to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not competent to decide about that anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But notwithstanding that, was there any other reason why you could not agree to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The atmosphere was not really conducive to any kind of signing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that you subsequently did sign it. Was this after there had been changes made to the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, these were all proposals, there was no definite written document that we had to sign, these were proposals which we had to formulate. Then we signed this document; there were three or four articles or paragraphs to that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us some of the other proposals that were suggested? If you can remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That the international rules of the Red Cross had to be respected; that hostilities should cease; that we would respect the agreement between Izetbegovic and Boban and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were detained in the cinema, were you ever taken out to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was to Rijeka, close to Vranjska. Those are the names of these localities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are just on the outskirts of Vitez, are they, close to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually this belongs to the municipality of Vitez and it is close to the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that took you out to dig these trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean by name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, do you know where these people came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were HVO members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any military activity going on around you during the time that you were digging the trenches, that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not notice any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard of anyone being subjected to any danger at that time when you were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were some people killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 26th April, do you recall a meeting being held where members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina arrived at the cinema?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was at the end of April. The commander of the BiH army, Sefer Halilovic, then Mr. Hasim Delic was there, Mr. Petkovic and Mario Cerkez, as far as I can recall. They were in the premises of the cinema, they entered the cinema hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of why they were there, why they had come to this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told that we would be released, that an agreement to that effect had been reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you were aware, they had come there for the purposes of negotiating for the release of the prisoners, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that when they came to the hall, that agreement had already been reached, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you ascertain, how did you find this out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the army commander wished us -- congratulated us on our freedom, wished us all the best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I said 26th April when I asked you the question, and I think you answered it was the end of April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that the date I suggested may have been incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the end of April that was. Whether it was the 29th, the 30th -- a lot of time has gone by and there were many things happening, so it is difficult to tell, but it was towards the end of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You feel that 26th April is too early, is not the right date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is too early. I think it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, it has in that statement the date 26th April, but do you now think that that may be the wrong date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could have said 29th, maybe an interpreter made an error or something, but I do not know, I think it was the end of April, that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After you had heard that some of these prisoners were to be released, did you see people that were released, did you hear of people being released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day or the next day, the majority were released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about 20 people stayed behind in the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay behind for in the cinema building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think for about three days, possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then taken somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to the chess club in Vitez, a building in which the chess club was located, on the ground floor and the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day were you taken there, day or morning, were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was about 3.00 am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you gain the impression that you were being taken there secretly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was dark. Possibly. Possibly one could have that impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately what date was it, can you remember? You may not remember, but approximately what date would it have been that you were taken to the chess club?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the 3rd, in the morning of the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is 3rd May, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 3rd May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you to the chess club?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By what means of transport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a minibus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were people from the cinema, I think there were about eight people from the cinema and another four from the SDK, the social accounting service. This was another building where people were detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you stay in the chess club?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 2.00 pm, we were taken to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the opstina of Busovaca, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in the opstina of Busovaca were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Kaonik, that is the name of that part of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a particular place in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a building that we were taken to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this building had been used for before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were military hangars, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say military before the war, that would have been the JNA, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been to Kaonik before this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, to the JNA barracks there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was never in those buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Kaonik, where were you placed and with whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were placed into cells in that building, we were driven to the building and then placed in a cell and there were a total of 13 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the 13 people that were with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, except for one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the room that you were put into, in terms of its size and description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was a room that was about 4.5 to 5 metres long by 3 metres wide. Along the longer wall, there was a bench to be used as a bed. There were no windows facing outside so there was no daylight, and there was a window facing the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were kept in this room, were you able to hear anything happening outside of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could hear the sounds of people wailing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear them saying anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could hear it, it was loud enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear what they were saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "I will tell everything", "don't, don't", things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After four days in Kaonik, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the Red Cross arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they arrived, did they come and see you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and we talked to them in the hallway. We even managed to write a message.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were held in Kaonik, were you ever interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was interrogated the following day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is after you had -- the following day after seeing the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in the town of Busovaca, at the premises of the insurance company there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were, I assume, the investigators there, there were several people who interrogated me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew one of them, I even had official business with him before. His name was Juresic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position he held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could assume that, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did he appear to hold, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they were investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what he did before the war, what position he had before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he also worked for the police in Zenica. He was in charge with protection from fire, from things like that and so we met on that basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnic group was he, did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time, during this period when you were being interrogated, did anyone else enter the room while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, other people came in and went out, that went on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who those people represented or where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally did not know these people, but they were all members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say or do anything to you while they were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones who interrogated me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the HVO that came into the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well yes, he said a few words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was giving me a pistol, so that I would kill myself, things like that. Then I said, "there is no need for that". Then he would offer me his pistol again and say, "okay then, you kill me", things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then taken back to Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was then returned to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then later interrogated in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well yes, the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who interrogated you in Kaonik the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact they gave me some paper, they posed some questions and the next day Zarko Petrovic interrogated me outside that building. It was very short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you spoken to Zarko Petrovic before this? Had you seen him before this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in fact he brought me in the car to the insurance company, then he drove me back from the insurance company, so he was involved in transportation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw him on the first occasion when you went to Busovaca and then you saw him again in Kaonik when he gave you the paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was also in the insurance company premises, he was also present there. Not all the time, but he was also present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say a piece of paper and they posed some questions. What were the questions they posed for you, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With whom I had contacts in Sarajevo, in Zenica. Then there was a question of my family ties with Izetbegovic, or my wife's ties with that family. The Vitez trade company, from whom of the Croats did we buy weapons, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke of Zarko Petrovic being at Kaonik on the next day. Was he the person that interrogated you in Kaonik on that day, or was it somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did that, but it was very short, in fact he just read what I had written down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you when he read the things that you had written down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not satisfied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then, when he was not satisfied? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean after my conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in the building, it was another building, it was about 100 metres away from the building where I had originally been brought, and in fact I stayed in a room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was kept there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Zarko Petrovic who brought me to this building and he left me in this room and there was a man at the reception desk, at the entrance to that building, and he left the keys with him and he told him not to let anybody in, into this room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told them not to let anyone in the room, Petkovic, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he told this man who was at this reception on duty, an older man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then a soldier came and asked him to unlock the room and he said that he did not have the keys, that he needed to go and ask the investigator, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the shift changed, that was around 7.00 or 8.00, that same man came again, and a new person on duty told him that he needed to ask the investigator in order to let him in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the man that came again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he later asked me, when he took me out of that room, whether I knew what his name was, that his nickname was Svabo and how come I did not know that he was that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the person that wanted to come into the room, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He did not do that until there was a change of shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the change of shift and when he came into the room, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took me out of that room and took me to another room. I think that this was like a dining hall, there were several tables and chairs there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into this dining hall, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I sat in a chair and he said just what I said before, he told me to say everything, everything I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started saying some things, he was not satisfied. I received several blows on my head and legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sitting in the chair at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he hit you in the head, did you stay in the chair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fell from the chair a few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from hitting you in the head, did he hit you anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in my legs and I received a hit in the kidney area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what did he hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no objects involved. Hands and kicks. He kicked me in my shins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any boots or shoes on his feet when he kicked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of this interrogation, did he produce any weapons of any sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a knife on his belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do with the knife, if anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took it out and then put it back and that was very brief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after the interrogation took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took me back to this room, that is the cell in this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then, after he took you back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a telephone there at the reception desk and then I heard him say, "director, everything is fine here".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he having a telephone conversation when he said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he use the word "director" or did he use some other word that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is the word he used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you suffer any injuries as a result of the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were bruises around my eyes and in the areas of my kidneys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, Zarko Petrovic came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zarko Petrovic say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said that he was not able to prevent this, that it was out of his control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell him what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I guess he saw. I assumed he knew, so that is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position Zarko Petrovic had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was an investigator, that is how they addressed him, so I think he was an investigator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some days later, were you spoken to by officials from an international organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the international organisation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The European Monitors, they were dressed in white, I think that they were the European Monitors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when it was that you were spoken to by the European Monitors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it was a day or two later after I was brought back from the second room, that was now the third cell. That was one or two days after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that you did not have a calendar with you when you were in prison, so it was difficult for you to keep track of the actual dates, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had other problems, so one does not think of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the European Monitors ask you any questions that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was something like, "how were you treated?", and things like that, how did people treat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked how you were treated, what did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was better not to say things to the monitors, so we said it was fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mention the fact that you had just been beaten a few days earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did not. I think I did not. It was visible, they could have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to see who it was, if anyone, that was accompanying the ECMM monitors as they were going around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that somebody was in front of -- I think there was somebody there. I do not know who it was, I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any officials from the camp, for example, going around with the ECMM monitors? That is people other than in the white uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were people who were present there, I do not know what their functions were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who the camp commander was at the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know at that time, but I know we signed a release document and we signed it in the presence of the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the camp commander's office was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know where the camp commander's office was, but we signed this document in the office that was in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the office that was in that building, relative to your cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Looking from the entrance to the building, it was to the left of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was in the same building as your cell was, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some days after the European Monitors made their visit there, did something then happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was the 14th and we were transferred to Vitez again to the cultural centre building and on 16th, the exchange took place; that is we were exchanged and then we were actually free.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the exchange take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I know that we were brought to Poculice. The UNPROFOR representatives were there as well as the ICRC. This is the part of the Vitez municipality controlled by the army, and that is where we were brought and that was the act of release, that was the final act of being set free.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit P7, if your Honours please? Mr. Kaknjo, would you look for me please at the document that has now been placed on that machine there? Make yourself comfortable so you can see it. It is not something, I know, you are familiar with, but would you just carefully look through it and if you see any names of any persons mentioned there that were in prison at the same time you were there, could you just indicate them by reference to the number? Any persons that you knew of that were in prison with you at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 15, Beso, I do not know if his name was Mustafa or not, but Beso was there yes, maybe it was not Beso -- Serif Osadsevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which number is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 64, 65, 67, 68, 69 but not that last name. Ramo Karijkic is 69. Number 70, 72, 73 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think 72 is a reference to you, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says "Fuad" here. 73, 74, 76. There was a Sefma there, I do not know his name, that would be 78.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the moment. We are going to have a break and we will resume work at 4.15. (3.55 pm) (A short break) (4.15 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, the witness is now at your disposal. Cross-examined by MR. MIKULICIC

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Kaknjo. I am attorney Mr. Goran Mikulicic, representing Mr. Zlatko Aleksovski in this case and it is my turn to ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going back to the part of your testimony when you said that Petrovic took you for interrogation and then brought you back to the Kaonik locality. You said that on that occasion, you were taken back to the building. Could you describe to us which building you are referring to? Did you manage to understand the purpose of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was returned to cell number 3, that is how it was marked. Before that, I was in cell 16. I was taken from cell 16 for interrogation and then taken back to cell 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person whom you called by his nickname Svabo, did he interrogate you in the same building to which you were taken back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in another building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe to us the building in question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the building of the intervention squad, because I saw people under arms there, who went to carry out operations, they were mentioning certain villages, so that I think this was the building where the intervention squad was accommodated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show us on an aerial photo of Kaonik the building you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if the picture is clear, I think I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to show the witness an aerial photograph which has been submitted as an exhibit, so that we can ask the witness to indicate the building where he was interrogated by a person nicknamed Svabo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the main road towards Busovaca, and this branches off towards Kaonik, so it would be this building (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photograph is not very clear. I think it was that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that building be marked, the building pointed to by the witness, as the building where he was interrogated by a person nicknamed Svabo. On this aerial photograph, can you discern the other building to which you were taken later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was this building (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this second building also be marked as the building identified by the witness. Do you know who was the commander of the intervention squad at the time when you were in that first building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not familiar with the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may be allowed, Mr. President, I think it would be desirable for the Prosecutor, who has another copy, to give this copy to the witness so that he can directly mark, put in the marks requested by the Defence, by counsel, and then it will be admitted as an exhibit of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Counsel would suggest that the first building be marked A and the second B, or in any other suitable way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: May I thank you for your suggestion, Mr. Mikulicic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Should I mark the picture?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do. So this would be building A, and the other one would be building B.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel would tender this aerial photograph thus marked into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is Exhibit D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kaknjo, you have described the, to put it mildly, unpleasantness you experienced in building A. You said that this building was actually the base of the intervention squad.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to all of us and the Trial Chamber what an intervention squad is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are people who intervene in certain situations. They engage in operations, they are given tasks to go to particular areas, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is in command of such an intervention platoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that an intervention platoon can be described as a military unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware what the function was of Zlatko Aleksovski at the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was the commander of the camp in Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you heard this person who beat you, Svabo, having a telephone conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who he was talking to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just heard what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though you said that once, would you be kind enough to repeat the exact words, as far as you can recollect them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Commander, it is okay, I have finished my job", words to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that all that you heard him say on the phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had visible injuries on the face from the blows you received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were bruises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall how many days after these events, after you were hurt, did the people whom you described as men in white, the European Monitors, come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A day or two later, very soon after that, because that period was full of events, it is rather hard to tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your recollection, could that visit have taken place on 10th May 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly, the 10th, the 11th, possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the person who was leading the European Monitors at the time in the Lasva River valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kaknjo, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No questions in re-examination, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Kaknjo, I have two questions for you. In your language, is the commander and director, are they two different things or can they be used to indicate the same thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In everyday terminology in peacetime, one could say "director" or "warden", but in a crisis situation, in wartime conditions, then "commander" or "director" could be used interchangeably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true that in those circumstances the most appropriate word would be "commander"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both terms could be used, either term could be used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My second question is as follows: do you know Mr. Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him on that day when we were going back to the cultural centre in Vitez, where we had been detained previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no real conversation, we just had to sign the release paper. We did not personally communicate, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether he is here? Could you point to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague Mr. Marchesiello will take the next witness. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could you please read your declaration. BAHTIJA SIVRO (sworn) Examined by MR. MARCHESIELLO

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can sit down please. Do you hear me? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name, age and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Bahtija Sivro, I was born on 27th January 1951 in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are you presently living, Mr. Sivro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacetd)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please could you tell us what is your nationality, Mr. Sivro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak, a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you describe yourself and your family from the point of view of ethnicity; you describe yourself as a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please briefly outline for the court your educational background, starting from high school on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I graduated elementary school in Vitez, secondary school of electrical engineering in Zenica and the electrical engineering faculty in Sarajevo, so I am a graduate electrotechnical engineer of the electronics specialisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a student and until graduation, did you have any political experience, party youth organisation and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not politically involved in any political organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At a certain moment in the subsequent years, did you take part in such a political organisation? Were you a member or are you still a member of a political organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At present I am a member of the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With which role and tasks, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am now just a regular member of the organisation, that is the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you join the party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain to the court the nature of this political organisation? What does SDA mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Party of Democratic Action in its title indicates democracy and it rallies mostly Bosniak Muslims, but there are members of other nationalities and confessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that there are Croats who can be members and actually are members of the party, of that party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have in the recent past or now do you have any administrative and/or governmental role in your country and/or in Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a time, I was head of the Bosniak section of the Vitez municipality after the signing of the Washington Agreement; or to be more precise, from October 1995 until the end of 1996, I held the position of head of the Bosniak section of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the court what you mean by "Bosniak section" of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately Vitez continues to be divided into two parts, the Bosniak part and the Croatian part, so that on both sides there are two heads, the head of the Croatian section and the head of the Bosniak section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still occupying this position, are you still mayor of Vitez, of the Bosnian part of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I no longer perform that function, I am now working in the government of the Central Bosnia canton in the Ministry of Industry and Power. I hold the post of Electrical Power Inspector and at the same time I am a delegate in the House of Representatives of the Parliament of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you briefly describe your professional history as a civilian and state your main professional experiences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon graduation from the university, I worked at the Zenica steel works as a young engineer. Shortly after that, I moved to Vitez and worked at the Vitezit enterprise as an engineer designer and after ten years of employment there, I became manager of engineering and development of the socially-owned enterprise called Vitezit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that Vitezit factory is part of a larger industrial complex in Vitez. Can you be more precise on this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these are chemical plants. In addition to Vitezit, there were two other companies that were quite separate. They operated independently, a company called Slobodan Princip Selo and another one called Sintevit and all three companies formed an association which used to belong to the business association of UNIS in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually in a physical sense they are a unit, they are in the same area, the three factories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are within the same compound and they form an entity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was on your arrival there and how, if you can say that, how has remained the situation of Muslim personnel within the factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite normal while I was working there from 1977 until the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: Sorry, they ask me to ask the court for a redaction from the transcript, page 87, line 17. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel is not quite aware what kind of redaction is in question, as we do not have the transcript before us. Could we be familiarised with this request?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Could you please, Mr. Prosecutor, explain this a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: Actually I cannot, because I have been asked to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are just seeking a redaction of something which we might write down on a piece of paper. If there is to be any discussion or debate about it, we should go into closed session. I will pass this over to Mr. Mikulicic, but if Mr. Mikulicic has any further discussion on it, I would be asking to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay, I am completely aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Are you agreeable, Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: I hope it has been only a technical accident and I hope it will not happen again. Can we start again with the last question? How was the situation with the Muslim personnel within the factory? I know you have already answered, but the other matter, the technical matter did not allow me to follow your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please specify what period you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the very beginning of your experience in the Vitezit to, let us say, mid 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have said already, there were no major problems regarding the position of Muslims working in that enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there more Muslims in the management of the company than Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More recently, that is in 1991/1992, the top management of all three firms consisted of Croats, in the majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, when did you first arrive in Vitez as a professional, as an engineer, to work there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the end of 1976 or the beginning of 1977.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you marry, could you please tell us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got married in 1978.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you last live in Vitez, in which area of Vitez did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in the downtown area, in a socially-owned apartment. I had an apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which part of divided Vitez is this area now? Is it in the Bosnian or the Croat area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apartment is in the Croat area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the collapse of former Yugoslavia and of the Communist regime, and until the end of 1991, could you tell us how were in Vitez the relations between the Croat and the Muslim communities? I am referring to your personal experience. Were there problems, conflicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1991, the Muslims and Croats lived together and they did not cause any difficulties for each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which was the structure of local government after the elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The structure of local government corresponded to the number of votes gained at the first elections that took place so that at those elections, more than 50 per cent was won by the Croats. They had a majority, and this was the result of the elections that took place in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time was there set up a Joint Council? Was it established at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there was a joint legislative and executive branch of government. The legislative was the municipal assembly and the executive was the executive council of the municipal assembly, which was the local government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November 1991, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, HZ-HB, was established. Did the situation you have briefly described to us, concerning the Muslims and the Croats in Vitez, start to change after that date, and in which terms, if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation after the formation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, in the first days or months, did not change much in Vitez, but there was an evident tendency on the part of the Croatian authorities to dominate over the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this tendency show itself? Can you give us some examples?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The government which was joint after the formation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croats sought to form the Croatian Defence Council and they succeeded in doing that at the beginning of 1992. The Muslims did not participate in that government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told about the establishment of the Croatian Defence Council, HVO. You described the main consequences of the establishment of the HVO in Vitez. Had there been at that time an attempt by the Muslims to find a peaceful way to co-operate with the Croats within these new structures that were being set up, I mean the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an attempt made in mid 1992, I think it was in June, if I recollect well. There was a joint session of representatives of the Croats, that is the main board of the HDZ of Vitez municipality, and the municipal board of the SDA of Vitez, together with all other people of goodwill and people who were prominent figures locally. Unfortunately, after two hours of debate and discussions, we did not succeed in reaching an agreement to form a unified government that would be called the Croatian Defence Council. The Muslims insisted that it be called the Croatian-Muslim Defence Council, and at the beginning, at this meeting, this seemed to be reasonable and even acceptable. However, this title was not accepted so that the Muslims did not wish to participate and did not participate in the Croatian Defence Council; that is in the local government by that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this meeting take place? Do you remember a particular place in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meeting was held in the amphitheatre of the elementary school, which was then called the Brotherhood and Unity Elementary School in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take part in the discussion and what in this case had been at that time your proposals for finding a reasonable settlement of the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I participated in the discussions at the meeting, expressing the will and desire for life together, and trying to avoid any disruption of life in Vitez municipality and, of course, I supported the position that the government should be called the Croatian-Muslim Defence Council, which regrettably was not accepted at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do the Muslim community react to this unhappy result of the meeting? Did they organise themselves autonomously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first they stayed on in the municipal building, but soon they were chased out of that building if they refused to sign allegiance to the government of the HVO. After that, self-organisation was resorted to, and a body was formed called the Co-ordination Committee for the Protection of Muslims. This body did not belong to any governmental institution or political organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of the members of this Muslim committee to organise defence? Some of them, at least?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember the names, such as Hasan Sadibasic, Nusret Kalco, Munib Kijmovic and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember Varupa Midhat as a member of that committee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of that body, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that during this period, the Croatians, to put it in a more precise way, the HVO, had already taken control of the most important institutions. Could you explain better in which forms did this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took over the police station, the post office building, the municipal building, and more or less all the public institutions that existed at the time, and this happened by force, they did this by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, what happened in your factory, in the Vitezit factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was working at the time as the manager for engineering and development, and the so-called civilian guards who were providing security for the plant were withdrawn and instead the HVO police were introduced, a special purpose police unit, which protected all the factories in the compound. This police force consisted exclusively of Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they put any flag or insignia on the factory, at the entrance of the factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the main entrance to the factory, the flag with the chequer board insignia was hoisted, which was a visible sign as to whom the factory belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember attending a military parade in the fall of 1992 at the local soccer stadium, and can you describe what happened on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I attended it briefly, where the local HVO unit gave the oath. I was there briefly, but I saw the entire ceremony on television immediately after that, that is the same night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the ceremony develop? Was there a parade, was there some oath taken by the troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, the units were on parade at the local stadium. They gave the oath and what I found particularly remarkable, the oath was given in words "Za Dom Spremni", "ready for homeland". In that period, this was reminiscent of World War II, where that movement was characterised as fascist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in command of the brigade on that occasion, the commander of the unit who was parading?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of these units was Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some major political representative give a speech in that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a public event and all local leaders of the Croatian Community were present, Dario Kordic, Pero Skopljak and others were present. I think that Tihomir Blaskic was there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I imagine they expressed the programme of that actions. Was there in their words any mention of the role that the Muslim community, minority, should have played in their new idea of the country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Among others, Dario Kordic also addressed these units, that is these soldiers. In my view, he had a very partial view about the role of the Croatian people, and the Muslim people were not mentioned in this speech. According to him, there were no Muslims, virtually, in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivro, do you remember what happened in Vitez and the surrounding area on 20th October 1992? You were there, you were in Vitez at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on 20th October, a minor incident happened in Vitez, and I would like to stress that it was an incident, not a conflict. There was a conflict in Novi Travnik, and the local leaders of both armies, which was then the Territorial Defence and the HVO, agreed not to get involved in the conflict in Novi Travnik. However, certain units coming from the direction of Busovaca, I think they were from Kiseljak and Busovaca, started in the direction of Novi Travnik. In the village of Ahmici, a barrier was put up in order to prevent these forces from coming to Novi Travnik. There was shooting, and I think that a member of the Territorial Defence was killed by a sniper on that occasion. The HVO units did not pass through to Novi Travnik, and the HVO took an exception to that, and pulled out the command of the Territorial Defence in Vitez and its logistics centre. Some of the people from this command were arrested and physically mistreated and four or five -- after four or five days, things were kind of settled and there were no more acts of provocation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this incident -- you said it was not a conflict in a proper military sense; did this incident produce consequences as to Vitez, in the sense of was Vitez divided and the division of Vitez you have mentioned, was this the first time that the town was divided into areas, into Croatian and Bosnian Muslim areas, and was it possible for Muslims to move freely from one area to the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, you could not speak about a division of the town, but the formations of the then Territorial Defence, and as I said the logistics centre, were forced to pull back to Stari Vitez, and after these changes, the Muslims did not feel safe living in Vitez. However, people still went on and about their business. They went to work and their life went on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean, if I understand well, that the Territorial Defence could not operate as a military unit out of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In general, how did the situation evolve from this period, October 1992, until April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this period, the situation was not good at all. The relations between Croats and Muslims kept deteriorating. There were constantly small local incidents. Business premises, shops and cafes, anything that was Muslim property, was destroyed either by explosives or by physical force. The Muslims, so to speak, were not free to conduct their business any longer in the urban part of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go to 15th April 1993. Was that a special day for the community, for the Muslim community in Vitez? Was it, and for which reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not call it a special day for the Muslim community, but it was a special day. On that day, the Territorial Defence grew into the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that was its official name, and that day was celebrated as the day of foundation or the establishment of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On that date, there was a small cocktail party in the fire fighters' hall in Vitez, and the representatives of the Croatian people were invited to this small celebration, both of the civilian and the military administration. The representatives did show up and took part in this small celebration. It looked as if we could have a communal life and that these conflicts and acts of provocation would not take place. This was very brief and with this cocktail party, this getting together of these groups actually came to a stop. I was present there on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there on the same day an announcement on TV, on Croatian TV, from the so-called crisis staff, and what was the content of this announcement? Was it on the same line of brotherhood and an expectance of peaceful co-existence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That evening, the local television of Vitez municipality broadcast a programme. This television was controlled by the Croats, the entire TV station. The following information was broadcast, that all misunderstandings and all incidents had been brought under control, and that people should go to bed with ease, that there will be no conflict between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the court briefly what were the functions and what was the composition of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that this was called "crisis staff" or "headquarters", and it was a military organisation. There were three representatives of the BiH army and three representatives of the HVO present there, and these were the leaders of the two respective organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went home and on your going home, did you notice something peculiar and curious or alarming on your way home that evening, after having heard about these two positive events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard of these positive events, but the town did not have a look of normalcy at all. There were very few people outside, there was something hanging in the air. Everybody feared the worst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you went home, you had your dinner with your family and you went to bed. What happened the morning after on April 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 16th April, I was wakened at 5.00 by powerful explosions that were heard very near the centre of town and there was sporadic fire from small arms. I woke up and I looked out of the window in the direction from where the sounds of explosions were coming, and I saw the surrounding villages were being attacked by mortar fire, by anti-aircraft weapons, and, of course, I saw fire and smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers and other military units -- was it possible to identify who was the attacker in that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, it was not clear to me exactly who was attacking, but since Vitez was, so to speak, under the HVO control, one could assume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the shelling -- did you notice the shelling in a specific direction? I mean, was it in the direction of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could not see Stari Vitez directly from my window, but by the sounds of the explosions, one could sense where these shells were falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in the building after the first explosions were heard? First of all, how many families were there in your area, in your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my building, that is the entrance where I lived, there lived 12 families and they were of mixed background. I think that there were four Muslim families, seven Croatian families and one Serbian family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in the building? Did you and your neighbours try to organise in order to protect your families and to have more information about what was going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we organised and we established a building watch in the front of the building, and the principle was that it would always be a mixed watch consisting of two persons. This went on for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during these three or four days, you remained in your apartment, except the time you were serving in the joint guards at the entrance of the building; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you get some information about what was going on? Which means did you have, except looking through the windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could receive information by telephone, because my telephone was still working. The local radio and television also gave certain information, and I could also receive the Radio Zenica programmes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you notice something, looking from the window, something specific, someone being killed or some dead body being transported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In those days, and in that period, I was receiving information that a certain number of people, that is Muslims, were being detained, or were killed; in other words that they were being detained or killed. Across the street from my building, the building where I used to live, I saw when the dead body of Midhat Varupa was brought out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the same Midhat Varupa you mentioned as a member of the Muslim committee to organise Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you recognise that that body was him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We already had information within the building that Midhat Varupa had been killed. After a while, the civilian protection people came and picked up his body. I knew that it was him because I knew exactly where he lived and I could see his hair when he was being brought out, because he had characteristic hair, it was blond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally, the inhabitants of the building, were you allowed to leave the building? Was it possible to get out and see what was going on during those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In those days, nobody was allowed to leave the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Was not allowed"; you mean in the sense that the situation was too dangerous, or that somebody had ordered you not to leave the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over the local radio, an order was given not to leave the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the building visited by the HVO in those days and before 19th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My building, that is my entrance, was not visited by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: I do not know if the court wants me to go on or if we have to resume the examination tomorrow. I have still many questions to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Maybe it would be a good idea to finish today. I do not know whether you have many questions to ask this witness. Would it be possible to finish today? I do not know. We can go on until 5.30. Would it be possible to finish by then?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that I am at about half of my examination. I do not know whether this is an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In that case, I think that we can take advantage of this interruption to adjourn, because we only have three more minutes left, and then we can resume work tomorrow. Are you agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCHESIELLO
utterances.text: Thank you. (5.30 pm)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
